title: Wasserstein Flow Matching: Generative modeling over families of distributions

nodes.text: Wasserstein Flow Matching (WFM) lifts flow matching onto families of distributions by exploiting the Riemannian structure of Wasserstein geometry, learning vector fields that act on the space of probability distributions rather than on points.
nodes.evidence: we propose Wasserstein flow matching (WFM), which appropriately lifts flow matching onto families of distributions by appealing to the Riemannian nature of the Wasserstein geometry

nodes.text: WFM is an instantiation of Riemannian flow matching (Chen and Lipman 2023) in which each individual sample is itself a probability distribution and the target velocity field matches the optimal transport map, i.e. the geodesic in Wasserstein space.
nodes.evidence: WFM is an instantiation of Riemannian FM (Chen and Lipman, 2023), where we train a neural model to learn a continuous normalizing flow (CNF) between distributions over distributions

nodes.text: The Wasserstein geometry, a canonical geometry over distributions, does not fit existing flow-matching frameworks (Euclidean, general manifolds, Fisher-Rao simplex, Dirichlet) and had not previously been successfully adapted for flow matching.
nodes.evidence: The Wasserstein geometry, a canonical geometry over distributions, does not easily fit into any of these existing frameworks and has not been successfully adapted for flow matching

nodes.text: Bures-Wasserstein Flow Matching (BW-FM) is a specialization of WFM to the Gaussian submanifold of Wasserstein space, using closed-form OT maps, exponential/logarithmic maps, and McCann interpolation between Gaussians.
nodes.evidence: In this case, we show that WFM can be further modified, resulting in the Bures–Wasserstein FM (BW-FM) algorithm

nodes.text: For point-cloud generation, WFM relies on transformer (attention) architectures whose permutation equivariance matches the equivariance of Wasserstein geometry, combined with entropic optimal transport to approximate OT maps between point-clouds.
nodes.evidence: two distinct, yet crucial, algorithmic primitives: (1) incorporating transformers in our neural network architecture... and (2) recent algorithmic advances in entropic optimal transport

nodes.text: Unlike denoising diffusion models, flow matching learns a deterministic continuous normalizing flow by regressing onto a simple conditional probability flow, with dynamics only simulated at inference (simulation-free training).
nodes.evidence: Unlike discrete time and probabilistic generative models (such as Denoising Diffusion Models by Song et al. (2020)), FM learns a deterministic, continuous normalizing flow

nodes.text: WFM differs from related distribution-over-distribution methods: Fisher FM and Categorical FM operate on the Fisher-Rao simplex geometry, and Meta FM (Atanackovic et al. 2024) requires pre-coupled distribution pairs, whereas WFM applies between two separate uncoupled distributions over distributions.
nodes.evidence: In contrast, we emphasize that our proposed Wasserstein FM applies between two separate uncoupled distributions over distributions

nodes.text: Existing point-cloud generative models (GANs, VAEs, normalizing flows, diffusion, Euclidean FM) are limited to uniformly sized 2D/3D point-clouds due to voxelization, and fail on high-dimensional spaces with variable-sized examples.
nodes.evidence: these approaches are limited to uniformly sized point-clouds in 2D & 3D, and fail on high-dimensional spaces which cannot be voxelized

nodes.text: WFM can perform generative modeling over Gaussian distributions to generate granular cell-state representations from single-cell genomics data, and over point-clouds to synthesize cellular microenvironments (niches) from spatial transcriptomics.
nodes.evidence: we generate representations of granular cell states from single-cell genomics data... synthesize cellular microenvironments from spatial transcriptomics datasets

nodes.text: On Gaussian-based datasets, BW-FM generates samples significantly more robust than naive approaches that ignore the underlying geometry, capturing covariances accurately even with few training samples while other methods produce degenerate covariances.
nodes.evidence: samples generated by our algorithm are significantly more robust than naïve approaches which do not fully exploit the underlying geometry of the data

nodes.text: For uniformly sized 3D point-clouds WFM is comparable to current generative models, but it uniquely succeeds in high-dimensional and inhomogeneous (variable-sized) settings where contemporary voxelization-based approaches fail.
nodes.evidence: For datasets of 3D point-clouds with uniform sizes, the performance of WFM is comparable to other current generative models... WFM succeeds in the high-dimensional and inhomogeneous settings

nodes.text: WFM uses the Benamou-Brenier / McCann interpolation formulation where geodesics in Wasserstein space are pushforwards of OT maps and the optimal velocity field is the time-derivative of the McCann interpolation.
nodes.evidence: we perform generative modeling in the Wasserstein space, where geodesics are given by pushforwards of optimal transport (OT) maps
